facts.text: Emporia, Virginia got its name from Emporia, Kansas, the hometown of Benjamin Tillar, a Virginia House of Delegates member.
In 1887, Emporia sprang to life when the towns of Hicksford and Belfield merged into a single city.
During the Civil War, the Petersburg Railroad ran through Emporia, becoming a strategic target as Union forces tried to cut off Richmond.
Today, Emporia sits where a CSX north–south line meets a former Norfolk Southern east–west track, echoing its historic crossroads role.
Three landmarks—Klugel Architectural Sheet Metal Work Building, Old Merchants and Farmers Bank Building, and Village View—are listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
